post_hoc_same_author_analysis.note: POST-HOC, not pre-registered. Of the 5 benign pairs matching or beating the organism pair, 4 are SAME-AUTHOR pairs (a3ilab-llm-uncertainty with itself x3, seong67360 with itself x1). The one different-author pair, Hwoooo x junejeong at 0.13115, is two repos both named task-36-Qwen-Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct -- the same fine-tuning exercise, so same-provenance in everything but account name.
post_hoc_same_author_analysis.why_this_is_post_hoc: The null was subset AFTER seeing which pairs beat the organisms. The pre-registered p against all 210 pairs is 0.0284 and that is the result; 0.0098 is a descriptive follow-up and is never quoted as the headline.

interpretation: The two organisms share a weight-space subspace at a level reached only by adapter pairs of common provenance. Per section 5 of the pre-registration, written before the run: this is evidence of COMMON PROVENANCE, not common objective. Both organisms come from one lab, one base, one rank, one synthetic-data pipeline, while the 21 controls come from 21 different authors, so this design cannot separate 'same loyalty' from 'same lab'. What it does establish is that shared origin between two suspect models is detectable from weights alone against a null of unrelated adapters -- a usable auditing primitive, and the first positive detection in this report.
